BaseSAP is an autonomous base-layer stealth address protocol designed for programmable blockchains like Ethereum.
It generates unique, random stealth addresses for recipients to conceal transaction linkability.
BaseSAP operates entirely at the application layer, requiring no core blockchain modifications.
The protocol is modular and supports multiple cryptographic schemes, including elliptic curve and lattice-based cryptography.
The prototype implementation uses the Secp256k1 elliptic curve and a dual-key stealth address protocol with view tags.
View tags reduce parsing time by approximately 86.84% compared to standard DKSAP.
BaseSAP improves parsing efficiency by about 50% relative to existing stealth address protocols.
Stealth addresses differ from CoinJoin and ZK-SNARKs by hiding recipient identity but not mixing funds or proving ownership anonymously.
BaseSAP addresses privacy challenges such as denial-of-service attacks and interoperability across blockchain frameworks.
The Dual-Key Stealth Address Protocol (DKSAP) separates spending and viewing keys for enhanced privacy.
BaseSAP's modularity enables future extensions to quantum-resistant cryptographic schemes.
Stealth addresses allow senders to generate ephemeral keys and shared secrets with recipients to create unlinkable addresses.
Recipients parse all ephemeral public keys on-chain to detect and spend from stealth addresses.
Potential applications include Smart Contract wallets, cryptocurrency donations, payroll, DeFi, public goods funding, and NFTs.
BaseSAP's design promotes decentralization, autonomy, and user privacy without requiring user interaction or censorship.
Elliptic curve Secp256k1 is widely used in cryptocurrencies and forms the cryptographic basis for BaseSAP's initial implementation.
BaseSAP publishes its codebase under an open-source license to ensure transparency and reproducibility.
The protocol was deployed and tested on Ethereum Goerli and Sepolia testnets as a proof of concept.
Stealth addresses do not obfuscate the flow of funds but hide the recipient's ownership within transactions.
BaseSAP aims to balance privacy with scalability and usability on public blockchains.
